RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Review of Regulations Regarding Abandonment and Discontinuance of Rail Lines and Rail Transportation Under 49 U.S.C. Section 10903
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: The Board’s statutes at 49 U.S.C. 10903-10905 govern abandonment of rail lines and discontinuance of rail service by common carriers. Specifically, section 10903 includes the procedures and standard for abandonment or discontinuance; section 10904 concerns offers of financial assistance for continued rail transportation; and section 10905 concerns offers for use of rail properties for certain public purposes. For these statutes, the Board has issued implementing regulations at 49 CFR part 1152, and that part also covers prospective use of railroad rights-of-way for interim trail use and rail banking. Chairman Fuchs intends to conduct a comprehensive, deregulatory review of these regulations to identify ways to streamline procedures, remove paperwork burdens, and strengthen evidence-related provisions.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Review of Regulations on Procedures Governing Ex Parte Communications
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: In 2018, the Board modified its regulations to permit, subject to disclosure requirements, ex parte communications in informal rulemaking proceedings. The Board also adopted other changes to its ex parte regulations that clarified and updated when and how interested persons may communicate informally with the Board regarding pending proceedings other than rulemakings. The intent of the modified regulations was to enhance the Board’s ability to make informed decisions through increased stakeholder communications while ensuring that the Board’s record-building process remained transparent and fair. Chairman Fuchs intends for the agency to assess whether additional changes to the Board’s ex parte regulations should be considered to further those goals and whether any changes are required to facilitate the Board’s compliance with Executive Order 14215, Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Review of Environmental Regulations
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: The Board has regulations implementing environmental laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), at 49 CFR part 1105. On January 20, 2025, President Trump issued Executive Order (EO) 14154, Unleashing American Energy, which directed the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) to propose rescinding CEQ’s regulations implementing NEPA and to provide guidance to agencies on implementing NEPA. CEQ published an Interim Final Rule (IFR) on February 25, 2025, in response to this direction, and the IFR became effective on April 11, 2025. 90 FR 10,610. Chairman Fuchs intends for the agency to fully comply with EO 14154, and--in light of the EO and CEQ’s IFR--the agency is reviewing the Board’s regulations implementing NEPA.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Review of Regulations Regarding Supplemental R-1 Reporting
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: In 2013, at the request of rail carriers, the Board amended its rules to require rail carriers that submit annual R-1 reports to identify information on capital and operating expenditures related to Positive Train Control (PTC). Those expenditures were expected to be high during statutorily-required PTC installation. Now that such installation is complete and the associated statutory deadline has passed, the burden of this paperwork exceeds its practical utility. Chairman Fuchs intends for the agency to take deregulatory action concerning unnecessary R-1 reporting.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

PUBLICATION.PUBLICATION_TITLE: Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Removal of Vacated Final Offer Rate Review Regulations
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: In a notice of proposed rulemaking issued September 12, 2019, the Board proposed a new rate case procedure for smaller cases, known as Final Offer Rate Review (FORR). Final Offer Rate Rev., EP 755 et al. (STB served Sept. 12, 2019). The Board issued a supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking regarding FORR on November 15, 2021, and adopted the final rule on December 19, 2022. Final Offer Rate Rev., EP 755 et al. (STB served Nov. 15, 2021 & Dec. 19, 2022) (with Board Members Fuchs and Schultz dissenting). On judicial review, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit held that the Board lacked statutory authority to prescribe rates through FORR and vacated the final rule. Union Pac. R.R. v. STB, 113 F.4th 823 (8th Cir. 2024), reh’g and reh’g en banc denied, Nos. 22-3648 & 23-1325 (8th Cir. Dec. 10, 2024). In light of the vacatur, Chairman Fuchs will pursue removal of the portions of 49 CFR parts 1002, 1111, 1114, and 1115 that were added by the final rule.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: First Time Published in The Unified Agenda

RIN_INFO.RULE_TITLE: Floating Cabins
RIN_INFO.ABSTRACT: To promote the unified development and regulation of the Tennessee River System, Congress directed TVA to approve obstructions across, along, or in the river system under Section 26a of the TVA Act. TVA also owns, as agent for the United States, much of the shoreland and inundated land along and under its reservoir system. In the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation Act of 2016, Congress established that TVA may establish health, safety, and environmental standards for floating cabins. There are approximately 2,200 floating cabins on the Tennessee River System. Floating cabin owners currently have until 2024 to comply with the standards and apply for a TVA Section 26a permit in order to remain on the Tennessee River System. Various factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic, supply chain and labor resource shortages, and wastewater certification decisions have caused delays for floating cabin owners to achieve compliance, and this proposal considers an extension of the deadline for all floating cabins owners to comply with the regulations and apply for a Section 26a permit along with clarifying amendments on the existing health, safety, and environmental standards.
RIN_INFO.RIN_STATUS: Previously Published in The Unified Agenda
